LESSON: READING 14.4.1 FEATURES OF STYLE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.4: Reading 14.4.1 Features of style
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 14.4.1 Features of style, part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use stylistic devices in writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text,  Search online and offline for examples of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in stories and them with the rest of the class. Control light intensity for Why do we use stylistic devices in writing? 141

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 14.4.1 Features of style in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use the styles of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in guided context,

Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views.  Read the class reader and identify with illustrations instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text, and display their work on the class notice boards. Learners who may not turn pages to use page-turners or be supported by peers. They could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to record findings.  Role-play selected dialogues from the class reader and record themselves for video 142 sharing and review. Ensure barrier-free access for learners with mobility difficulties. Safety for all learners should be observed. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 14.4.1 Features of style together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Self-efficacy is developed as the learner holds a discussion on instances in real life where dialogues, similes, and

metaphors can be used, thereby enhancing their literary skills.

 Learning to learn is achieved as the learner interacts with technology when recording and sharing videos of selected

dialogues from the class reader.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates others when role-playing selected dialogues.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Critical thinking is achieved as the learner relates use of the features of styles in real life.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates features of style in the study of class readers to the learning of readers in Kiswahili.
